releaseStatus: local implementation verified; no release requested or deployed

selection.name: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)
selection.basis: Focus an existing English cloud-fundamentals set on an international IT learning audience. Existing 23 questions, official learning references and working review/resume features provide a practical starting point.
selection.limits: Keyword volume, country-specific demand and overseas retention were not measured. This change adds study content; it does not establish traffic or revenue growth.

content.nature: Original English scenarios with four choices, one correct answer, an explanation and an official per-question learning reference. Independent practice; not an official exam paper, full test simulation or score predictor.
content.preserved: All 111 previous topic groups and the original 23 Azure questions match the recorded baseline. Existing question IDs, choice IDs, version, archived content and other catalog entries remain unchanged.
content.storage: Existing public authored-content overlay. No database writes, migrations or hosted service configuration changes.

coverage: All 70 new question IDs resolve through the API with an answer, explanation and official reference; wrong-exam requests and page 6 return 404.
The English directory and all five set pages, question outlines and updated counts render without JavaScript.
A returning learner retains the former three-question second-page progress and bookmark; a new question supports grading, explanation, bookmark, reload, mistake review and a direct link.

verification.dbAuthFixtures: Not configured. Ten DB/Auth-related browser tests were skipped; those flows were not verified by this run.
verification.cleanup: After all 74 browser cases finished, Windows server teardown remained pending. The verified Next child listening at 127.0.0.1:3100 was stopped; Playwright reported 64 passed and 10 skipped, the six monetization scenarios passed, and check:local exited 0. Build-generated next-env.d.ts changes were restored to the pre-task state.
